chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masrur (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn 'Amir narrated to us, from his uncle 'Abdullah ibn 'Amir, from Muhammad ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Aban ibn 'Uthman, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever takes on my religion, travels my path, and follows my tradition, then let him profess the superiority of the Imams from my Ahl al-Bayt over all of my nation, for indeed their likeness in this nation is like that of the Gate of Remission among the Children of Israel.

key_terms.أهل بيتي: My Ahl al-Bayt - the Prophet's household, referring to his family lineage
key_terms.الائمة: The Imams - the divinely appointed leaders from the Prophet's household
key_terms.باب حطة: Gate of Remission (Bab Hitta) - a gate the Children of Israel were told to enter humbly for forgiveness, referenced in Quran 2:58
key_terms.تفضيل: Superiority/preference - recognizing the higher station of the Imams
key_terms.منهاجي: My path (minhaj) - the clear way or methodology of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the Imams of Ahl al-Bayt and the Gate of Remission?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) instructs his followers that adherence to his religion, path, and sunnah necessitates recognizing the superiority of the Imams from Ahl al-Bayt over the rest of the Muslim community. He compares them to the 'Gate of Remission' (Bab Hitta) that God commanded the Children of Israel to enter in humility for forgiveness (Quran 2:58), implying that allegiance to the Imams is a gateway to divine mercy and salvation. This hadith was narrated through a Qummi-Kufi chain via the Companion Ibn 'Abbas.
